title: Fairness Theatre: Evaluating Post-Hoc Fairness Interventions in Vendor-Controlled Early Warning Systems
abstract: arXiv:2609.38552v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Public institutions increasingly procure AI systems whose design they cannot inspect or change. In higher education, proprietary Early Warning Systems (EWS) leave colleges with few options beyond adjusting model outputs to address inequity. This raises the question of how fairness work is coordinated among vendors, institutions, advisors, and students with unequal power to change these systems? Using student records from a public college in Ontario, Canada, we evaluate six post-hoc fairness interventions on a research EWS under simulated procurement constraints. We compare fairness, accuracy, and demographic disparities, introducing error-type profiling to trace how interventions redistribute false positives and false negatives. Interventions redistributed disparities without consistently reducing them. Two implementations favored already-advantaged groups because they used group size to define disadvantage; small, marginalized groups

translated_title: 公平性剧场：在供应商控制的早期预警系统中评估事后公平性干预措施
translated_abstract: 公共机构越来越多地采购其无法检查或修改设计的AI系统。在高等教育领域，专有的早期预警系统（EWS）使高校除了调整模型输出以应对不公平问题之外几乎没有其他选择。这就提出了一个问题：在供应商、院校、顾问和学生这些改变系统能力不对等的主体之间，公平性工作是如何协调开展的？我们利用加拿大安大略省一所公立学院的学生记录，在模拟采购约束的条件下，在一个研究用早期预警系统上评估了六种事后公平干预措施。我们比较了公平性、准确性和人口群体间差异，并引入了错误类型剖析方法来追踪干预措施如何重新分配假阳性和假阴性错误。研究发现，这些干预措施只是重新分配了群体间差异，而未能持续地减少差异。其中两种实现方式由于使用群体规模来定义劣势地位，反而有利于原本已处于优势地位的群体；而规模较小的边缘化群体……
tldr: 本研究在模拟采购约束下评估了六种事后公平干预措施，发现这些干预只是重新分配而非持续减少群体间差异，且基于群体规模定义劣势的方法反而有利于优势群体，揭示了供应商控制系统中“公平性剧场”式的局限。
en_tdlr: Evaluating six post-hoc fairness interventions on an early warning system under simulated procurement constraints, this study shows that such interventions redistribute rather than consistently reduce disparities, with group-size-based methods even favoring already-advantaged groups, exposing what the authors call "fairness theatre."
